Container.Name: subtitlarr
Container.Overview:
Fills gaps in your Bazarr subtitle library by translating subtitles you already have (e.g. English) into languages you're missing (e.g. Spanish), using a local or cloud LLM. Never mounts your media folders — all reading and writing of subtitles happens through Bazarr's own REST API, so Bazarr remains the only thing with filesystem access to your library.
Everything except the port and data path below is configured from the web UI after first start — Bazarr connection, translation engines (Ollama, llama.cpp, Gemini, NVIDIA NIM, OpenRouter, Groq), scheduling, and all other settings persist in Subtitlarr's own database, not container environment variables.
No media path needs to be mapped into this container — only the /data path below, which is Subtitlarr's own small SQLite database, not your library.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Host port mapped to the container's internal port 7777 — keep this matching 7777 on both sides. Unraid's built-in Tailscale hook auto-configures Serve to proxy to the HOST-mapped port number, so a mismatched mapping (e.g. a different host port than the container's actual internal port) breaks the Tailscale hostname URL even though local/LAN access still works fine.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Subtitlarr's own SQLite database (queue, run history, settings, engine instances). NOT a media path — do not point this at your library.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID the app runs as inside the container — must own (or have write access to) the Data path above. Unraid's default 'nobody' user is 99.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID the app runs as inside the container. Unraid's default 'users' group is 100.
